# SdH spot check

## What
A fixed-(n, D) magnetic-field sweep over a **low-field window**, designed to resolve
Shubnikov–de Haas / quantum-oscillation **frequency content** at one density — the
onset field and the tone frequencies — by FFT in 1/B. Mechanically this is a
`field-sweep-1d` (see it for the Station / sweep / fp / plot call surface); what
makes it a *spot check* is the design discipline below — the field range, 1/B spacing
Δ(1/B), and settling are chosen to resolve the tones cleanly, and the read is the 1/B
FFT.
It is the cheap 1D precursor to a `landau-fan`: one density, but **full per-point
quality**.

## When
- **Before committing a `landau-fan`.** A spot check pins the **onset** (sets the
  fan's B-range), the **observed tone frequencies** (confirm/correct the fan's
  Δ(1/B)), and the **settling/sensitivity** the fan inherits. A fan is the dense
  version; a couple of clean spot checks de-risk it — and can answer the question
  outright (`investigations/trilayer-stacking-fs-count.md` Step 3).
- Whenever a `field-sweep-1d` or `gatemap` showed QO-like wiggles and you want the
  frequency content at a point, not the whole (n, B) plane.

## Why
A spot check is cheap because it is **one density (1D), not because it is
low-quality**. Its whole value is being acquired *well* — at the settling floor and
Nyquist on the fastest tone — so a clean spot check can be decisive on its own and a
noisier fan cannot overturn it (`landau-fan`). Two knobs carry the quality:

- **Sampling.** The fastest tone sets the finest 1/B period. The reference frequency
  **F_L = (h/g·e)·n** (g = 4) — what a single four-fold pocket carrying all the
  density would give — is an upper bound on the fastest tone; Nyquist it. Undersampling
  the fast tone folds its aliases into the low-frequency band, where they masquerade
  as a small/slow tone (Verify).
- **Settling.** A swept-point dwell has a floor near the lock-in time constant
  (dwell ≥ k·τ; k ≈ 5 at 6 dB/oct, 7–10 at 24 dB/oct). Under-settling **attenuates
  the oscillation amplitude itself** (the filter cannot track the QO) — benign on a
  smooth slope, but it *buries a small tone* (Verify). The floor is non-negotiable
  when the target is a weak tone.

## Recipe
1. **Density + range.** Pick the density — high |n| gives the most periods and the
   clearest tones. Sweep a field window **[B_lo, B_hi]** sampled **uniformly in 1/B**
   (`field_invB`), not in B: SdH oscillations are periodic in 1/B, so even spacing there
   gives constant points-per-period and FFTs the raw points (no resample). `B_lo` is a
   small positive floor (~0.1–0.3 T) below the expected **onset** — uniform-1/B is
   densest in B at low field, so it captures the onset (the lowest B where oscillations
   emerge once the MR background is subtracted) for free.
2. **Δ(1/B) from F_L.** Compute F_L = (h/4e)·n and Nyquist-resolve it: Δ(1/B) ≤ 1/(2·F_L)
   (prefer 1/3). Set N from the window: N = (1/B_lo − 1/B_hi)/Δ(1/B) + 1. This Δ(1/B)
   (and N) is what a committed fan inherits.
3. **Lock-in.** Set sensitivity so full scale ≈ I_bias × R_target — a signal at a
   few % of range is coarse-ADC digitized (the grainy-FFT failure). Set the dwell at
   the settling floor (Why); read τ and the filter slope, do not guess them.
4. **The sweep.** Run it as a `field-sweep-1d` (its Recipe is the call surface):
   build the Station, ramp the gates to (n, D), `s.sweep(mag.field,
   field_invB(B_start, B_end, N), delay=dwell)`, fp the temperature(s) and every
   lock-in X/P, plot the live MR and gate-current leakage.
5. **FFT read.** Re-form Rxx from the TSV (rendered PNGs alias).
   - **Onset** — `hera.analysis.sdh_onset(R, B)` returns an `SdhOnset`: `onset_b` and
     `clip_high_b` (the low/high field edges bounding the usable window),
     `b_centers`/`snr`/`peak_freq` (the per-window curves behind the onset, ordered
     high-B → low-B, for picking the cutoff below), and `consensus_freq` (the high-B
     reference tone the SNR band tracks).
   - **FFT** — `hera.analysis.sdh_fft(R_grid, B, *, b_range=(cutoff, B_max), bg_degree=5)`
     removes the MR background with a degree-`bg_degree` polynomial **in B** (the
     background is smooth in B, not 1/B), then FFTs in 1/B, and returns
     `(freqs, magnitude)` with `freqs` in Tesla. It needs a field range wide enough that
     the polynomial captures the background without absorbing the oscillations.
     `cutoff ≥ onset_b`, and often **above** it (Verify). Read the **tone frequencies**
     against F_L.

## Verify
- **Settling — under-settling buries a small tone.** A dwell below the floor
  attenuates the oscillation amplitude (the filter can't track it). On a smooth slope
  that's a benign uniform lag; when the target is a small/weak tone it *erases* the
  feature. Non-negotiable for a weak-tone hunt; bend it only for a slope read on a
  strong signal.
- **Sampling — an undersampled fast tone aliases down.** If Δ(1/B) under-samples the
  fastest tone (≈ F_L), its aliases fold into the low-frequency band and masquerade
  as a small/slow tone. Nyquist the *fast* tone even when the target is the slow one
  (worked case: Examples).
- **FFT stability sweep.** Vary `bg_degree` and the window; a real peak **sharpens**
  as the 1/B record lengthens, an alias/artifact **wanders**.
- **Onset is read from the background-subtracted data, not the FFT.** It is the
  low-field point where oscillations emerge in ΔRxx(B) (the MR background removed), not
  a quantity the FFT returns. It is a **lower bound** on the FFT low-field cutoff:
  residual background near the low-B end inflates the slowest tones, so raise the cutoff
  above the onset until the slow-tone amplitudes stop shrinking. Report the onset — it
  sets a fan's B-range and tracks quantum mobility (a rise on a later cooldown is a
  device-quality regression).

## Examples
- *(our-measurement, QC0426/VTI 2026-06-16)* — at n = +8×10¹² a **12.5 mT** spot check
  resolved two tones (a main tone + a low-frequency partner) summing to F_L, where a
  same-session fan run at a coarser B-step and under-settled did not. A prior **50 mT**
  step had under-sampled the ~83 T main tone, folding its aliases into the small-tone
  band. The worked case for "acquire the spot check well, *then* commit the fan."

## Next
- **Clean QO, tones resolved** → run a `landau-fan`, inheriting this spot check's
  Δ(1/B), settling, and onset; or take a couple more spot checks across density for a
  cheap preview of the n-dependence.
- **Two tones at D ≈ 0** → `investigations/trilayer-stacking-fs-count.md` (the
  FS-count combinatorics).
- **Tone amplitude vs T wanted** (effective mass) → `temperature-dependence`
  Flavor B.

1	# Gatemap
2	
3	## What
4	2D raster sweep over an axis-aligned rectangle in `(V_tg, V_bg)`-space at
5	zero field, via `s.megasweep(k_tg.volt, ..., k_bg.volt, ...)`. All lock-in
6	channels read at every grid point; gate-current channels monitored for live
7	leakage. The first map you take when cap ratios `dtg` / `dbg` are not yet
8	trusted — sweeping in raw gate voltages avoids any `(n, D) ↔ (V_tg, V_bg)`
9	calibration error. Plots via
10	`sharpelab_nb.plotting.plot_gatemap(file_path, file, nD=True)` (the analysis
11	side reprojects to physical `(n, D)` after the fact, using the cap ratios
12	in scope at plot time — separate from the sweep itself).
13	
14	For the polygon-in-`(n, D)` variant (rasterized parallelogram via
15	`raster.rasterize` + `multisweep`), see `nD-map`. The two recipes share
16	external structure (AsyncStation, fp/plot, comments) but differ in their
17	sweep call and their cap-ratio dependency.
18	
19	## When
20	Once the device-init validators are in place: hard dependency is
21	`gate-current-sanity-check` with Cell B committed (the safe `(V_tg, V_bg)`
22	ranges define the maximum extent of the megasweep box) and, for
23	rhombohedral devices, `silicon-backgate-survey` (`V_si` is held at the
24	operating point this gatemap commits to). A `gate-leakage-survey` should
25	have been done already — or, for any gatemap that ventures far from
26	`(0, 0)`, have a leakage-check `register_run_before` callback installed
27	(see `gate-leakage-survey` Flavor B). After the first gatemap is in hand,
28	the campaign branches by scientific question (see `## Next`).
29	
30	The natural predecessor of `nD-map`: a clean axis-aligned gatemap is the
31	substrate from which `cap-ratio-calibration` extracts the CNP slope, which
32	is what makes a polygon-in-`(n, D)` sweep trustworthy.
33	
34	## Why
35	The gatemap is the only measurement in the toploader pipeline that surveys
36	the gate plane densely without committing to a particular feature or to a
37	particular set of cap ratios. Every downstream Block 1 recipe targets a
38	specific point or line — and you can only pick one if you've seen the
39	map. A 201×201 megasweep at `slow_delay=3, fast_delay=1` takes ~3.5 hours
40	and is the densest first-look you can get without dropping into
41	rasterized-polygon sweeps (`nD-map`).
42	
43	The axis-aligned form has two failure modes the polygon form doesn't:
44	(1) it wastes 30–60% of points outside the safe polygon when the
45	`(n, D)` region of interest is a tilted parallelogram, and (2) on a
46	device with strongly-coupled top/bottom gates, a rectangle in
47	`(V_tg, V_bg)` is a sheared parallelogram in `(n, D)` and the CNP cuts
48	the rectangle diagonally. Both are worth tolerating on the *first* map,
49	because the alternative requires cap ratios you don't yet trust.
50	
51	## Recipe
52	
53	1. Decide the `(V_bg, V_tg)` extent. Stay strictly inside the validators
54	   set by the device-init recipes; for a first gatemap pick a rectangle
55	   that brackets the working setpoint with margin (e.g.
56	   `V_bg ∈ [-8, 6.5]`, `V_tg ∈ [-6.5, 6.5]` for a 25.5/16 nm device at
57	   `V_si = 48 V`).
58	2. Build `s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)`. `s.add_comment('gatemap')` first,
59	   then optional structured tags identifying the operating point, e.g.
60	   `s.add_comment(f'MC{N}, Vsi = {V_si}V')`. Call
61	   `s.add_comment(grab_metadata())` if the notebook has the helper (RPL_19
62	   idiom — captures device/run state into the comments list).
63	3. `s.ramp` all relevant gates and the field to their start values.
64	   `time.sleep(10)` (or `interruptible_sleep(30)` for a slower settle when
65	   `V_si` just moved).
66	4. `fp` temperature (and `fridge_temperature` if available), all three
67	   gate currents, and every lock-in `X` and `P`. `plot` `k_bg.volt` vs
68	   `k_bg.curr` and `'time'` vs `k_tg.curr` / `k_si.curr` so live leakage
69	   is visible; for a survey gatemap also `s.plot(k_bg.volt, sr.X)` over
70	   each lock-in.
71	5. (Optional) `s.register_run_before(autorange_sr830s, [sr830s_2_autorange])`
72	   if you want sensitivity to track during the slow axis. Aaron typically
73	   leaves this commented out for the canonical 201×201 — autorange
74	   disturbs the lock-ins mid-fast-row. With autorange off (the canonical
75	   choice), set each voltage lock-in's sensitivity to the **largest
76	   resistance you need to resolve**, and fold in the voltage preamp gain G
77	   from the card: the lock-in sees V_xx×G, so a sensitivity sized from the
78	   bare V_xx under-ranges by G and clips R_max. Use sens ≳ R_max × I_ac × G
79	   with ~×2 headroom.
80	6. `s.megasweep(k_tg.volt, np.linspace(V_tg_lo, V_tg_hi, 201), k_bg.volt, np.linspace(V_bg_lo, V_bg_hi, 201), slow_delay=3, fast_delay=1)`.
81	   Slow-axis convention varies — Aaron's recent style is TG slow, BG
82	   fast (cf. RPL_19/20251220 cell 70); RPL_10/241207 used BG slow, TG
83	   fast. Either works; the analysis-side `plot_gatemap(..., nD=True)`
84	   reprojects to `(n, D)` regardless.
85	7. Park gates: `k_bg.volt(0); k_tg.volt(0)`. (Don't park `V_si` unless
86	   you're done with this `V_si` entirely.) Send a Discord/Slack ping
87	   (`alerts.discord('🐍jobs done🐍')`) if the alert hooks are installed.
88	
89	## Verify
90	
91	Post-hoc disk checks. The map's `data/<file_id>/` directory has
92	`metadata.json`, `data.tsv.gz`, and `plot.png`. The `Run` loader unrolls
93	the 2D megasweep into flat rows, so column-wise statistics work the same
94	way they do for 1D sweeps.
95	
96	```python
97	from hera.analysis import open_run, summarize_run
98	import numpy as np
99	
100	run = open_run("<notebook_dir>/data/<file_id>")
101	print(summarize_run(run))
102	# expect: type 2D, recipe 'gatemap', complete (rows == n_slow * n_fast),
103	#         tags carrying MC label / Vsi.
104	
105	# 1. Sweep completeness — interrupted sweeps usually mean leakage abort or
106	#    operator stop; treat as block until the human explains.
107	assert not run.interrupted, "sweep was interrupted; investigate before advancing"
108	
109	# 2. Leakage stayed below threshold across the whole map. Threshold matches
110	#    the gate-leakage-survey abort thresholds (~5e-11 to 8e-11 A); use 1 nA
111	#    as a soft ceiling and surface anything closer than 100 pA.
112	i_tg_max = np.abs(run.col("k_tg_curr")).max()
113	i_bg_max = np.abs(run.col("k_bg_curr")).max()
114	assert i_tg_max < 1e-9 and i_bg_max < 1e-9, (
115	    f"leakage exceeded 1 nA: |I_tg|={i_tg_max:.3e}, |I_bg|={i_bg_max:.3e}"
116	)
117	if max(i_tg_max, i_bg_max) > 1e-10:

# Gatemap

## What
2D raster sweep over an axis-aligned rectangle in `(V_tg, V_bg)`-space at
zero field, via `s.megasweep(k_tg.volt, ..., k_bg.volt, ...)`. All lock-in
channels read at every grid point; gate-current channels monitored for live
leakage. The first map you take when cap ratios `dtg` / `dbg` are not yet
trusted — sweeping in raw gate voltages avoids any `(n, D) ↔ (V_tg, V_bg)`
calibration error. Plots via
`sharpelab_nb.plotting.plot_gatemap(file_path, file, nD=True)` (the analysis
side reprojects to physical `(n, D)` after the fact, using the cap ratios
in scope at plot time — separate from the sweep itself).

For the polygon-in-`(n, D)` variant (rasterized parallelogram via
`raster.rasterize` + `multisweep`), see `nD-map`. The two recipes share
external structure (AsyncStation, fp/plot, comments) but differ in their
sweep call and their cap-ratio dependency.

## When
Once the device-init validators are in place: hard dependency is
`gate-current-sanity-check` with Cell B committed (the safe `(V_tg, V_bg)`
ranges define the maximum extent of the megasweep box) and, for
rhombohedral devices, `silicon-backgate-survey` (`V_si` is held at the
operating point this gatemap commits to). A `gate-leakage-survey` should
have been done already — or, for any gatemap that ventures far from
`(0, 0)`, have a leakage-check `register_run_before` callback installed
(see `gate-leakage-survey` Flavor B). After the first gatemap is in hand,
the campaign branches by scientific question (see `## Next`).

The natural predecessor of `nD-map`: a clean axis-aligned gatemap is the
substrate from which `cap-ratio-calibration` extracts the CNP slope, which
is what makes a polygon-in-`(n, D)` sweep trustworthy.

## Why
The gatemap is the only measurement in the toploader pipeline that surveys
the gate plane densely without committing to a particular feature or to a
particular set of cap ratios. Every downstream Block 1 recipe targets a
specific point or line — and you can only pick one if you've seen the
map. A 201×201 megasweep at `slow_delay=3, fast_delay=1` takes ~3.5 hours
and is the densest first-look you can get without dropping into
rasterized-polygon sweeps (`nD-map`).

The axis-aligned form has two failure modes the polygon form doesn't:
(1) it wastes 30–60% of points outside the safe polygon when the
`(n, D)` region of interest is a tilted parallelogram, and (2) on a
device with strongly-coupled top/bottom gates, a rectangle in
`(V_tg, V_bg)` is a sheared parallelogram in `(n, D)` and the CNP cuts
the rectangle diagonally. Both are worth tolerating on the *first* map,
because the alternative requires cap ratios you don't yet trust.

## Recipe

1. Decide the `(V_bg, V_tg)` extent. Stay strictly inside the validators
   set by the device-init recipes; for a first gatemap pick a rectangle
   that brackets the working setpoint with margin (e.g.
   `V_bg ∈ [-8, 6.5]`, `V_tg ∈ [-6.5, 6.5]` for a 25.5/16 nm device at
   `V_si = 48 V`).
2. Build `s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)`. `s.add_comment('gatemap')` first,
   then optional structured tags identifying the operating point, e.g.
   `s.add_comment(f'MC{N}, Vsi = {V_si}V')`. Call
   `s.add_comment(grab_metadata())` if the notebook has the helper (RPL_19
   idiom — captures device/run state into the comments list).
3. `s.ramp` all relevant gates and the field to their start values.
   `time.sleep(10)` (or `interruptible_sleep(30)` for a slower settle when
   `V_si` just moved).
4. `fp` temperature (and `fridge_temperature` if available), all three
   gate currents, and every lock-in `X` and `P`. `plot` `k_bg.volt` vs
   `k_bg.curr` and `'time'` vs `k_tg.curr` / `k_si.curr` so live leakage
   is visible; for a survey gatemap also `s.plot(k_bg.volt, sr.X)` over
   each lock-in.
5. (Optional) `s.register_run_before(autorange_sr830s, [sr830s_2_autorange])`
   if you want sensitivity to track during the slow axis. Aaron typically
   leaves this commented out for the canonical 201×201 — autorange
   disturbs the lock-ins mid-fast-row. With autorange off (the canonical
   choice), set each voltage lock-in's sensitivity to the **largest
   resistance you need to resolve**, and fold in the voltage preamp gain G
   from the card: the lock-in sees V_xx×G, so a sensitivity sized from the
   bare V_xx under-ranges by G and clips R_max. Use sens ≳ R_max × I_ac × G
   with ~×2 headroom.
6. `s.megasweep(k_tg.volt, np.linspace(V_tg_lo, V_tg_hi, 201), k_bg.volt, np.linspace(V_bg_lo, V_bg_hi, 201), slow_delay=3, fast_delay=1)`.
   Slow-axis convention varies — Aaron's recent style is TG slow, BG
   fast (cf. RPL_19/20251220 cell 70); RPL_10/241207 used BG slow, TG
   fast. Either works; the analysis-side `plot_gatemap(..., nD=True)`
   reprojects to `(n, D)` regardless.
7. Park gates: `k_bg.volt(0); k_tg.volt(0)`. (Don't park `V_si` unless
   you're done with this `V_si` entirely.) Send a Discord/Slack ping
   (`alerts.discord('🐍jobs done🐍')`) if the alert hooks are installed.

## Verify

Post-hoc disk checks. The map's `data/<file_id>/` directory has
`metadata.json`, `data.tsv.gz`, and `plot.png`. The `Run` loader unrolls
the 2D megasweep into flat rows, so column-wise statistics work the same
way they do for 1D sweeps.

```python
from hera.analysis import open_run, summarize_run
import numpy as np

run = open_run("<notebook_dir>/data/<file_id>")
print(summarize_run(run))
# expect: type 2D, recipe 'gatemap', complete (rows == n_slow * n_fast),
#         tags carrying MC label / Vsi.

# 1. Sweep completeness — interrupted sweeps usually mean leakage abort or
#    operator stop; treat as block until the human explains.
assert not run.interrupted, "sweep was interrupted; investigate before advancing"

# 2. Leakage stayed below threshold across the whole map. Threshold matches
#    the gate-leakage-survey abort thresholds (~5e-11 to 8e-11 A); use 1 nA
#    as a soft ceiling and surface anything closer than 100 pA.
i_tg_max = np.abs(run.col("k_tg_curr")).max()
i_bg_max = np.abs(run.col("k_bg_curr")).max()
assert i_tg_max < 1e-9 and i_bg_max < 1e-9, (
    f"leakage exceeded 1 nA: |I_tg|={i_tg_max:.3e}, |I_bg|={i_bg_max:.3e}"
)
if max(i_tg_max, i_bg_max) > 1e-10:
    print(f"⚠️  approaching leakage threshold: |I_tg|={i_tg_max:.3e}, |I_bg|={i_bg_max:.3e}")

# 3. Lock-in channels not stuck or saturated. Flat-zero or flat-nonzero on
#    every channel is the grounded-device failure mode (cf. gate-current-
#    sanity-check failure-mode catalog); flat anything is suspicious for a
#    map that's supposed to vary across (V_tg, V_bg).
for name in ("sr830_1_X", "sr830_2_X", "sr830_3_X", "sr830_4_X"):
    if name not in run.cols:
        continue
    x = run.col(name)
    if np.allclose(x, x[0]):
        raise RuntimeError(f"{name} is flat across the map — check lock-in / wiring")
    if np.isnan(x).any():
        raise RuntimeError(f"{name} has NaNs — sweep aborted mid-row?")

# 4. Eyeball the rendered plot — Read('<notebook_dir>/data/<file_id>/plot.png').
#    The gatemap's qualitative features (CNP line slope, dome shapes, flavor
#    transitions) are easier to assess visually than numerically; the
#    numeric checks above are necessary, not sufficient.
```

If a CNP-line extraction or feature catalog is needed downstream, defer
that to `gatemap-feature-locator` (separate recipe). The Verify block
here is just "is this map clean enough to advance from".

## Examples
- `aaron/RPL_19/20251220_measure.ipynb` cells 69–76 — canonical mature
  form. Cell 70 is the 201×201
  `s.megasweep(k_tg.volt, np.linspace(-6.5, 6.5, 201), k_bg.volt, np.linspace(-8, 6.5, 201), slow_delay=3, fast_delay=1)`
  at `V_si = 48 V` using `mc_9`; cell 71 reverses the slow axis (sweep
  direction check). Cell 72 is a markdown interlude ("THink there is a
  problem with a bnc t so swapping that out"); cell 73 retries cell 71's
  range. Cells 74–75 are silicon-backgate-survey forms (`V_si` as slow
  axis with `np.linspace(48, -48, 101)` — strictly belongs to
  `silicon-backgate-survey`, included here because the same `# Gatemap`
  markdown header parents them). Cell 76 is the same 201×201 at
  `V_si = -48 V`. The `add_comment('MC6, Vsi = -48V, gate map')` plus
  `add_comment(grab_metadata())` is the canonical comment idiom; this
  recipe's slug is now `gatemap` rather than the older `'gate map'`
  freeform string.
- `aaron/RPL_10/241207_measure.ipynb` cells 43–53 — first-cooldown form,
  predates the mature shape. Cell 43 is the markdown header; cells 44–53
  are 10 megasweeps over progressively-refined `(V_tg, V_bg)` rectangles
  at `V_si = +10, -10, +20 V`. Cell 44 omits the `s.ramp(k_si.volt, ...)`
  (V_si already at default); cells 46–47 add the explicit ramp + sleep.
  Cell 48 is `V_si = -10 V`; cells 51–53 are `V_si = +20 V`. Notable:
  each cell carries `s.add_comment('initial gatemap, V_si = 10')` —
  Aaron's `add_comment` discipline begins exactly here in this notebook
  (gate-checks at cells 22–42 had none). The autorange callback is
  commented out for these runs.

## Next
Default branches by what you saw on the map:
- **Cap ratios not yet trusted (or first cooldown of this device)**:
  `cap-ratio-calibration` — extract CNP slope from this gatemap, refine
  `dtg` / `dbg`. Required before any `nD-map` you want to trust.
- **Caps already trusted, want a denser polygon survey**: `nD-map` over
  the `(n, D)` parallelogram of interest.
- **No clear features at this V_si**: revisit `silicon-backgate-survey`
  for a different operating point.
- **Features visible, want them at finite field**: `gatemap-in-field`
  (the same shape with `s.ramp(mag.field, B)` first; bake settling time
  in for a strong magnet).
- **Specific point looks SC / AHC / flavor-transition-shaped**:
  `field-sweep-1d` to characterize how that feature responds to B at
  fixed gate; `gate-axis-linecut` for a denser 1D cut along an n- or
  D-line through the feature.
- **Suspect history dependence (asymmetric or noisy-looking gatemap)**:
  `hysteresis-check` along an n-line through the feature.
- **Want a ranked list of candidate features to follow up**:
  `gatemap-feature-locator` (HERA-side analysis).

Block 2 branches once Block 1 is exhausted: `landau-fan` (B × n at
fixed D), `temperature-dependence`; deferred: `fraunhofer` (B × bias at
fixed gate), `bias-spectroscopy`. Reach for these only after the
zero-field map is well-characterized.

3. **Run the designated checks.** The canonical pair (the card may
   designate others):
   - a 1D gate-response sweep — qualitative: smoothness, leakage floor,
     feature visibility. Useful even with no reference trace; judged on
     its own terms.
   - a short cut through a known feature with a designated reference
     trace — quantitative; this is the check that carries the verdict.
   Tag every run `s.add_comment('reentry-baseline')` plus a structured
   comment naming the reference being reproduced.
4. **Compare quantitatively** — four checks, numbers not eyeball:
   - **resistance scale**: ratio to reference at matched points;
   - **feature positions**: shift of CNP/peak/dip locations along the
     swept axis;
   - **trace shape**: overlay; same feature set, same ordering — a
     missing or extra feature is a shape fail even at matched scale;
   - **leakage / drain-current floor**: at or below the reference's.
   Pass bands come from the designated pack's own README where it has
   one; otherwise propose bands from the reference's noise/repeatability
   and say so (heuristic, stated — not silent judgment).
5. **Verdict, then the handshake.** State pass/fail per check and the
   overall call in the notebook. Disagreement is **stop-and-report** —
   surface the specific check, magnitude, and candidate explanations,
   and wait; it is the operator's call whether the session recalibrates,
   investigates, or accepts the change as the new baseline. Do not
   silently recalibrate to the new behavior: an accepted change must be
   recorded (device card + a structured comment), because it becomes the
   *next* session's reference.

## Examples

- `zack/20260610-QC0426-hera-live` runs 0–2 *(our-measurement)* — the
  motivating gap: the first live VTI session ran exactly this procedure
  at gate C (gate-response sweep + density-cut reproduction against a
  curated `./reference/` pack with a four-check README) but had no slug
  for it; the runs are tagged under `gate-current-sanity-check` and
  `trilayer-stacking-id`, and the session notes flagged the missing
  recipe. This file is that flag's resolution.
- QC0426 device card, gate-C section *(our-measurement, mechanical)* —
  the reference-pack convention, including its correction history: the
  first designated references were bad picks (cable-swapped sweeps; a
  cut taken at 6 T) and were superseded by a curated pack on the session
  wiring at B = 0. Lesson encoded in step 2: a reference is only valid
  for comparison under reproduced conditions, and reference *selection*
  is part of campaign design — a bad pick fails the baseline spuriously.

## Next

- **Pass**: the campaign's first recommended recipe; the verdict line in
  the notebook is the record that gate C closed.
- **Fail / changed**: stop-and-report (step 5). Depending on the
  operator's ruling, the usual follow-ups are `gate-range-finding`
  (validator re-verification if gate behavior moved) or
  `gate-leakage-survey` (if the leakage floor moved); an accepted change
  updates the device card and the designated references.
- **No references designated and none exist**: this was a first session
  in disguise — switch to the device-init sequence.

# Gate current sanity check

## What
A sanity check at the start of a cooldown: sweep each active gate from 0 out
to each of its previously established card limits (others parked at 0),
watching gate current at pA resolution — does it leak, or does it look safe?
Safe → move on. Leaks → stop and report. Not a leakage test; a quick
liveness-and-gross-safety pass before the campaign starts.

## When
Once per cooldown, after instrument init and the measurement-config block,
before any subsequent recipe. Optionally also after thermal cycling or
physical intervention (reseating contacts, swapping a bias source).

**Preconditions:**
- Card-provided gate limits exist (device card, or a prior `gate-range-finding`).
- Gates ungrounded, device in a measurable configuration.

## Why
This is the cooldown's liveness check, run before any measurement because
everything downstream assumes it holds: the device is alive — passes a
measurable current — and every gate stays clean across the range the campaign
will use. The gate validators are already committed (the gate-validators slot,
from the card); this check confirms the device is actually safe within them. A
gate that leaks within its range is a data and device-safety problem. This is
a liveness and gross-safety check, not a leakage test: characterizing a
leakage onset is `gate-leakage-survey`, re-deriving the range is
`gate-range-finding`.

## Recipe

Two cells. HERA proposes both together. The human runs Cell A once — it loops
every leg (each gate × both polarities), each leg getting its own file and
slug — watching the live gate-current plot, then runs Cell B once. No
copy-the-cell iteration: the legs are enumerated up front.

### Cell A — gate sweep

Sweeps every active gate from 0 to each of its card limits, other gates
parked at 0. `nplci=10` on the gate-current channels for high-SNR pA
readback (~167 ms/pt); it stays at 10 across the sweep, Cell B resets it.

```python
# === Gate sweep: every active gate, 0 -> each of its card limits ===
# Endpoints = the device-card gate limits set as TG_MIN/TG_MAX, BG_MIN/BG_MAX in the
# gate-validators slot. Nothing to hand-substitute.
# Watch the live gate-current plot per leg: pA, riding the charging slope = safe.
# A gross turn-up off that slope = it's leaking -> Kernel Interrupt (the try/finally
# parks the gate); stop and report (skip Cell B).

# one leg per gate per polarity, (gate, endpoint)
legs = [
    (k_tg, TG_MAX), (k_tg, TG_MIN),
    (k_bg, BG_MAX), (k_bg, BG_MIN),
]
n_pts   = 251
delay   = 1            # s
lockins = [sr830_1, sr830_2, sr830_3, sr830_4]   # match your mc

# pA-floor readback on the gate-current channels; Cell B resets to 1.
k_tg.nplci(10)
k_bg.nplci(10)

# AC sense drive ~1 nA (liveness current) via the device-card drive->current relation
# — don't inherit the lock-in's residual amplitude (it starves the X read).
sr830_1.amplitude(<amp for ~1 nA per device card>)

for gate, v_endpoint in legs:
    s = sweep.AsyncStation(measurement_config)
    s.add_comment('gate-current-sanity-check')
    s.add_comment(f'gate: {gate.name}')
    s.add_comment(f'leg: 0 -> {v_endpoint:+g} V (card limit)')

    # park gates at 0 (the swept one starts from 0)
    s.ramp(k_tg.volt, 0)
    s.ramp(k_bg.volt, 0)

    xp = gate.volt
    # temperature: fp it per the rig card's polling rules
    s.fp(k_tg.volt).fp(k_tg.curr)
    s.fp(k_bg.volt).fp(k_bg.curr)
    s.plot(xp, k_tg.curr)
    s.plot(xp, k_bg.curr)
    for lia in lockins:
        s.fp(lia.X).fp(lia.P)
        s.plot(xp, lia.X)

    try:
        s.sweep(gate.volt, np.linspace(0, v_endpoint, n_pts), delay=delay)
    finally:
        s.ramp(gate.volt, 0)
```

Each leg's endpoint is a device-card gate limit — the `TG_MIN/TG_MAX`,
`BG_MIN/BG_MAX` set in the gate-validators slot — so there are no limit numbers
to hand-substitute; HERA just lists the legs. The `lockins` list should match
the channels in your `measurement_config`; if `mc` lists exactly the active
sr830s HERA may pre-fill it, otherwise the human sets it.

Read the live plot per leg:
- Lock-in `X`: nonzero, smoothly varying → device alive.
- Swept gate `*.curr`: stays in pA, on the capacitive charging slope, to the
  limit → safe.
- Parked gate `*.curr`: at the readback floor → no cross-gate path.

A geometry-derived ceiling (≈ ±0.5 V/nm × hBN thickness for the metal gates)
sanity-checks the card limits themselves: if a card limit exceeds it, treat
the card as suspect — don't sweep to it, flag to the operator before running.

### Cell B — reset nplci

After every leg has run, reset gate-current `nplci` back to standard. Only run
this if every leg looked safe; if anything leaked, stop and report instead (a
leaking gate is `gate-leakage-survey`'s problem, not this recipe's).

```python
# === Reset gate-current nplci ===
# Validators were already committed in the gate-validators slot — nothing to re-commit.
# Undo Cell A's nplci bump; print the live validators to confirm.
k_tg.nplci(1)
k_bg.nplci(1)

print("k_tg.volt validator:", k_tg.volt.vals)
print("k_bg.volt validator:", k_bg.volt.vals)
```

### HERA handshake

HERA proposes Cell A (all legs) and Cell B together, and **does not propose
any subsequent recipe step until the human reports the per-leg results.** If
everything looked safe HERA moves on; if any gate leaked HERA stops and
reports — it never advances on a gate that leaked. Human is the gate; HERA
waits.

### Failure-mode catalog

| What you see on the live plot | What it means | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Lock-in `X` nonzero and smoothly varying | Device alive, contact wiring good | Continue |
| Lock-in `X` flat zero on one channel | Wiring break on that contact pair | Stop; check wiring |
| Lock-in `X` flat-nonzero, **all channels at the same value** | Device tied to ground (shared-node short) — false signal that mimics readback | Stop; unground the device, then re-run Cell A |
| `k_*.curr` saturated at full-range readback (e.g. ±1 µA on `rangei=1e-6`) | Range too coarse for the leakage scale, or a real leak that pinned the range | Drop `rangei` to `1e-9` and re-run; if still saturated, real leak |
| `k_*.curr` makes a gross turn-up off the capacitive charging slope | It's leaking | Interrupt; stop and report (don't run Cell B); `gate-leakage-survey` to characterize |
| Parked gate `*.curr` tracks the swept gate | Cross-gate leakage path | Stop; characterize via `gate-leakage-survey` |

## Examples

- `aaron/RPL_10/241207_measure.ipynb` cells 22–25 — an early one-shot
  liveness check: three small fixed `0 → +1 V` sweeps (TG, BG, Si BG),
  full-range sweeps deferred to separate per-gate recipes. The canonical
  liveness shape; the loop here generalizes it to the card limits.
- `isaac/b1c2_toploader/20260505_measure.ipynb` cells 17–27 — first live
  HERA test, an early version of this recipe in action. Cell 22 is the sweep cell with
  `nplci=10` (using the older save/restore pattern). Hit the grounded-device
  failure mode (cell 26 diagnoses: sr830_2/3/4 share contact 30, all locked
  to ground potential). After ungrounding, manual range-finding established
  `k_tg.volt = (-7, +6)` and `k_bg.volt = (-4, +4.4)`; cell 27 commits the
  validators. The session also surfaced that `KEITHLEY_DEFAULTS["rangei"]`
  should be `1e-9` for pA-resolution; the b1c2 template was patched
  in-session.

## Next

- **Safe**: move on to the campaign's next recipe — every gate swept clean to
  its card limit on each side, and the `add_comment` slug captured the recipe
  identity in metadata.
- **Leaks**: stop and report; the operator decides whether to characterize via
  `gate-leakage-survey` or re-derive limits via `gate-range-finding`.
- **Results not reported**: HERA will not advance.

1	# Field sweep 1D
2	
3	## What
4	Sweep the magnetic field from one setpoint to another at fixed (V_tg, V_bg) (and fixed V_si, fixed bias), reading every lock-in channel along the way. The simplest measurement in the toploader pipeline that varies field, and the natural follow-up when a `gatemap` or `nD-map` reveals a feature you want to characterize as a function of B. Plots via `sharpelab_nb.plotting.plot_sweep(file_path, [file], ...)`. Two distinct usage modes:
5	- **"Linecut in field" mode** (Aaron) — pick an (n, D) point that looked interesting in a gatemap, ramp the gates, run a tight sweep over a small B range to look for AHC switching, SC critical fields, etc.
6	- **"Full-range MR" mode** (Bingcheng) — no gates, fixed angle/orientation, sweep B over the full ±10/±12 T range to characterize the magnetoresistance landscape.
7	
8	## When
9	After the validators are blessed and after at least one `gatemap` / `nD-map` / `gatemap-in-field` has revealed a feature worth probing. For Bingcheng's gateless rotator workflow, the dependency simplifies to "instruments are initialized, rotator is at the desired angle." Often run repeatedly inside one session, sweeping the same gate point over progressively wider B ranges (cf. RPL_19 "AH Spot Checks"): the same `Station` is reused across many cells.
10	
11	## Why
12	Cheap (10–60 minutes per sweep), highly informative, and the only measurement that resolves SC critical fields, hysteresis-switching fields, weak-localization peaks, and other field-axis features with full B-axis density. A 2D `gatemap-in-field` sees one B value; a 1D field sweep sees the whole axis at one (n, D) point. The two modes are complementary.
13	
14	## Recipe
15	**Common shape — single Station built once, reused across many sweeps:**
16	1. Build `s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)` (or `sweep.Station(mc)` for Bingcheng's synchronous workflow).
17	2. Compute the target (V_tg, V_bg): `Vtg, Vbg = calculate_gate_voltages(n, D, dtg=..., dbg=...)`. Skip if you're in Bingcheng's gateless mode.
18	3. `s.ramp(sr830_1.amplitude, A)` to set excitation; `s.ramp(k_tg.volt, Vtg); s.ramp(k_bg.volt, Vbg)`; `s.ramp(k_si.volt, V_si)`; `s.ramp(bias_voltage.volt, 0)` if a DC bias source is present. `s.ramp(mag.field, B_start)` to position the magnet at the start of the first sweep. `time.sleep(10)` (or longer for high field).
19	4. `s.add_comment('field-sweep-1d')` then optional structured tag identifying the gate point: `s.add_comment(f'(Vtg, Vbg) = ({Vtg}, {Vbg}), n = {n}, D = {D}')` (parseable by `comment_to_gates` if you use the `'label: (Vtg, Vbg)'` form). For RPL_19 idioms, also `s.add_comment(grab_metadata())`.
20	5. `fp` temperature(s), all three gate currents (or just gate voltages if Isaac's idiom), and every lock-in X / P. `plot` `mag.field` vs each lock-in X (the live magnetoresistance trace) plus `'time'` vs each gate current (live leakage).
21	6. (Optional, recommended for high-bandwidth runs) `s.register_run_before(autorange_sr830s_v2, (sr830_4, sr830s_2_autorange,))` so sensitivity tracks the trace.
22	7. **The sweep — multiple cells, same Station**: `s.sweep(mag.field, np.linspace(B_start, B_end, N), delay=0.5)`. Each subsequent cell is just another `s.sweep(...)` call — Aaron's idiom is to escalate the range on each cell ("`np.linspace(0, 0.1, 101)`", "`np.linspace(0.1, -0.1, 101)`", "`np.linspace(-0.1, 0.2, 201)`", etc.), bumping the bounds outward as features appear. Each `s.sweep` produces one file. The Station is *not* rebuilt between cells — the comments accumulate, the fp/plot list persists.
23	8. **End**: `mag.field(0)` (or wherever the next section needs it), `k_bg.volt(0); k_tg.volt(0)` if done with this gate point.
24	
25	**Notes on cadence:**
26	- Aaron uses `delay=0.5` for fast field sweeps (101 points × 0.5 s = ~1 minute), `delay=1` for slower scans where Hall channel needs more averaging.
27	- Bingcheng uses `delay = 3 * time_constant` (with `time_constant = 1` s, that's 3 s/point × 4801 points × ±12 T × 5 mT step = ~4 hours per sweep). The slower cadence is justified by the 5 mT B-step resolution he wants for hysteresis-feature visibility.
28	- For paired forward/backward at the same gate (a hysteresis check by another name), see `hysteresis-check`.
29	
30	**Notes on field source plumbing:**
31	- AMI430-controlled magnet: `mag.field` is the canonical parameter; `mag.field(B)` sets, `mag.field()` reads. Ramps respect the AMI430's internal ramp rate.
32	- Yokogawa-controlled magnet (`yoko_mag` in RPL_19/20251220+): same parameter surface, but the Yoko has a write-only software cache (see `sharpelab_nb.drivers.Yokogawa7651`). After a kernel restart, seed the cache via `set_voltage_cache()` / `set_current_cache()` or pass `start=` to ramp methods, or the ramp will raise.

# Field sweep 1D

## What
Sweep the magnetic field from one setpoint to another at fixed (V_tg, V_bg) (and fixed V_si, fixed bias), reading every lock-in channel along the way. The simplest measurement in the toploader pipeline that varies field, and the natural follow-up when a `gatemap` or `nD-map` reveals a feature you want to characterize as a function of B. Plots via `sharpelab_nb.plotting.plot_sweep(file_path, [file], ...)`. Two distinct usage modes:
- **"Linecut in field" mode** (Aaron) — pick an (n, D) point that looked interesting in a gatemap, ramp the gates, run a tight sweep over a small B range to look for AHC switching, SC critical fields, etc.
- **"Full-range MR" mode** (Bingcheng) — no gates, fixed angle/orientation, sweep B over the full ±10/±12 T range to characterize the magnetoresistance landscape.

## When
After the validators are blessed and after at least one `gatemap` / `nD-map` / `gatemap-in-field` has revealed a feature worth probing. For Bingcheng's gateless rotator workflow, the dependency simplifies to "instruments are initialized, rotator is at the desired angle." Often run repeatedly inside one session, sweeping the same gate point over progressively wider B ranges (cf. RPL_19 "AH Spot Checks"): the same `Station` is reused across many cells.

## Why
Cheap (10–60 minutes per sweep), highly informative, and the only measurement that resolves SC critical fields, hysteresis-switching fields, weak-localization peaks, and other field-axis features with full B-axis density. A 2D `gatemap-in-field` sees one B value; a 1D field sweep sees the whole axis at one (n, D) point. The two modes are complementary.

## Recipe
**Common shape — single Station built once, reused across many sweeps:**
1. Build `s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)` (or `sweep.Station(mc)` for Bingcheng's synchronous workflow).
2. Compute the target (V_tg, V_bg): `Vtg, Vbg = calculate_gate_voltages(n, D, dtg=..., dbg=...)`. Skip if you're in Bingcheng's gateless mode.
3. `s.ramp(sr830_1.amplitude, A)` to set excitation; `s.ramp(k_tg.volt, Vtg); s.ramp(k_bg.volt, Vbg)`; `s.ramp(k_si.volt, V_si)`; `s.ramp(bias_voltage.volt, 0)` if a DC bias source is present. `s.ramp(mag.field, B_start)` to position the magnet at the start of the first sweep. `time.sleep(10)` (or longer for high field).
4. `s.add_comment('field-sweep-1d')` then optional structured tag identifying the gate point: `s.add_comment(f'(Vtg, Vbg) = ({Vtg}, {Vbg}), n = {n}, D = {D}')` (parseable by `comment_to_gates` if you use the `'label: (Vtg, Vbg)'` form). For RPL_19 idioms, also `s.add_comment(grab_metadata())`.
5. `fp` temperature(s), all three gate currents (or just gate voltages if Isaac's idiom), and every lock-in X / P. `plot` `mag.field` vs each lock-in X (the live magnetoresistance trace) plus `'time'` vs each gate current (live leakage).
6. (Optional, recommended for high-bandwidth runs) `s.register_run_before(autorange_sr830s_v2, (sr830_4, sr830s_2_autorange,))` so sensitivity tracks the trace.
7. **The sweep — multiple cells, same Station**: `s.sweep(mag.field, np.linspace(B_start, B_end, N), delay=0.5)`. Each subsequent cell is just another `s.sweep(...)` call — Aaron's idiom is to escalate the range on each cell ("`np.linspace(0, 0.1, 101)`", "`np.linspace(0.1, -0.1, 101)`", "`np.linspace(-0.1, 0.2, 201)`", etc.), bumping the bounds outward as features appear. Each `s.sweep` produces one file. The Station is *not* rebuilt between cells — the comments accumulate, the fp/plot list persists.
8. **End**: `mag.field(0)` (or wherever the next section needs it), `k_bg.volt(0); k_tg.volt(0)` if done with this gate point.

**Notes on cadence:**
- Aaron uses `delay=0.5` for fast field sweeps (101 points × 0.5 s = ~1 minute), `delay=1` for slower scans where Hall channel needs more averaging.
- Bingcheng uses `delay = 3 * time_constant` (with `time_constant = 1` s, that's 3 s/point × 4801 points × ±12 T × 5 mT step = ~4 hours per sweep). The slower cadence is justified by the 5 mT B-step resolution he wants for hysteresis-feature visibility.
- For paired forward/backward at the same gate (a hysteresis check by another name), see `hysteresis-check`.

**Notes on field source plumbing:**
- AMI430-controlled magnet: `mag.field` is the canonical parameter; `mag.field(B)` sets, `mag.field()` reads. Ramps respect the AMI430's internal ramp rate.
- Yokogawa-controlled magnet (`yoko_mag` in RPL_19/20251220+): same parameter surface, but the Yoko has a write-only software cache (see `sharpelab_nb.drivers.Yokogawa7651`). After a kernel restart, seed the cache via `set_voltage_cache()` / `set_current_cache()` or pass `start=` to ramp methods, or the ramp will raise.

The `add_comment` carries the (Vtg, Vbg) tuple in `comment_to_gates`-parseable form: `f'..., (Vtg, Vbg) = ({vtg}, {vbg})'` — Aaron-style structured tagging at its best.
- `aaron/RPL_19/20260124_measure.ipynb` cells 41–53 — mature linecut-in-field mode, ±B escalating sweeps. Cell 42 is the canonical full setup cell: AsyncStation, `s.ramp` to (n=0.465, D=1.000), `s.add_comment('MC6, Vsi = 48V, gate map in -100 mT')` (stale text — actual setpoint is 0 T at cell start, ramping to 0.1 T mid-cell), `fp`/`plot` block, autorange callback installed (`s.register_run_before(autorange_sr830s_v2, (sr830_4, sr830s_2_autorange,))`), then `s.sweep(mag.field, np.linspace(0, 0.1, 101), delay=0.5)`. content.content:
1	# Landau fan
2	
3	## What
4	2D map of carrier density × magnetic field at fixed displacement field: `mag.field` as the **slow** axis of a `multimegasweep`, with a paired-(k_tg, k_bg) n-line (fixed D, via `calculate_gate_voltages(ns, Ds, dtg=..., dbg=...)`) as the **fast** axis:
5	```python
6	s.multimegasweep([mag.field], [B_vec], [k_tg.volt, k_bg.volt], [Vtgs, Vbgs], slow_delay=1, fast_delay=0.9)
7	```
8	Field is slow because gates are cheap to retrace and the magnet is not — the magnet ramps once, monotonically, across the whole fan. Every lock-in X/P read at each grid point. Analysis side plots B vs n (`pcolormesh`) per contact pair and overlays Středa lines (see Verify). Distinct from its two neighbors: `field-sweep-1d` is one gate point with full B-axis density; `gatemap-in-field` is the full 2D gate plane at a *single* B. The fan trades both for the (n, B) plane — the only measurement that resolves how gapped states *disperse* with field.
9	
10	## When
11	Three triggers, in rough campaign order:
12	- **Oscillation check** — a `field-sweep-1d` or `gatemap-in-field` showed quantum-oscillation-like wiggles and you need to know if they're real. The corpus idiom is literally named for this: RPL_19's "Small fan to check if oscillations are real" (a 161 × 151 fan after an effective-mass series kept hinting at SdH). A feature that moves systematically across the n-line as B steps is physics; one that doesn't is noise or gate drift.
13	- **State classification** — a map shows a vanishing-ρxx region (or a busy set of dips) and the discriminating question is whether the features disperse. This is the classification backbone of an FQAH/SC-style campaign (arXiv 2504.06972: ρxx(ν_h, B) fans + Středa fits are how (R/F/I)QAH states were separated from the SC region).
14	- **Calibration** — SdH/LL frequency vs n gives cap ratios independently of the CNP-slope method, and for a moiré device the fan anchors the moiré density n_M. The extraction is `cap-ratio-calibration`'s job (deferred — recipe not yet written); the fan is its input data.
15	
16	Prerequisites are `nD-map`'s plus a field-verified magnet: cap ratios `dtg`/`dbg` must be trusted (the fast axis is a line in (n, D) — wrong caps tilt it), and the field source must be live (Yokogawa cache seeded after kernel restart, AMI430 in operating mode — see `field-sweep-1d` plumbing notes).
17	
18	## Why
19	A dip in ρxx at one B value is ambiguous — gap, SC, contact artifact, density wobble. The same dip tracked across a fan is nearly unambiguous: a gapped state at fixed filling traces a straight line in (n, B) whose slope *is* its Chern number (Středa: dn/dB = C·e/h), an SC pocket sits at fixed n and dies at moderate B without dispersing, and quantum oscillations fan out with 1/B periodicity that yields the Fermi-surface area. One measurement, three discriminations, plus calibration for free.
20	
21	The cost is real: these are the most expensive sweeps in the corpus. Reference wall-clocks *(our-measurement, toploader, non-blocking-magnet era — the formula below them omits the traverse term; do not carry these numbers to another rig untagged)*: RPL_10's 101 B × 101 n fan at `slow_delay=30, fast_delay=1` took **4.3 h** (file 156); the 351 × 251 version took **27.8 h** (file 159); RPL_19's 161 × 151 at `fast_delay=0.6` took **5.5 h** (file 1776 — Aaron's own `# 1776, took 5.5 hours` annotation propagates through later fan cells); the 441 × 231 fan to 5 T took **30.1 h** (file 1840). Aaron's inline arithmetic (`(351*501)/(201*151)*3` in 20260124 cell 134) is the toploader-era form.
22	
23	**Estimate before you run — the full cost model**: wall-clock = **field-traverse time + N_rows × (row turnaround + N_fast × per-point time)**. Which term dominates is a rig property, not a constant of nature: **if the field source is ramp-rate-limited and the set call blocks** (check the rig card for whether yours is), the traverse term is fixed by the B-span alone — **finer B steps cost only row turnaround, and coarsening B buys aliasing, not time**. Traverses come in two species, priced differently: a **bare ramp** moves at the magnet's ramp rate; a **measured traverse** (the same leg recorded as a sweep) moves at an effective rate degraded by per-point overhead. A "free" measured ramp-down is usually still worth taking — it buys data for wall-clock — but it is not free: price it at the measured rate, from the rig card's Timing rules (`rig_card.md`), never the bare one. Calibrate row turnaround and per-point time from this session's own first sweeps; inherited timing constants carry a provenance tag and the conditions they were measured under, or they are guesses.
24	
25	## Recipe
26	1. Pick the n-window and fixed D from the map that motivated the fan, and decide the B span. # Landau fan

## What
2D map of carrier density × magnetic field at fixed displacement field: `mag.field` as the **slow** axis of a `multimegasweep`, with a paired-(k_tg, k_bg) n-line (fixed D, via `calculate_gate_voltages(ns, Ds, dtg=..., dbg=...)`) as the **fast** axis:
```python
s.multimegasweep([mag.field], [B_vec], [k_tg.volt, k_bg.volt], [Vtgs, Vbgs], slow_delay=1, fast_delay=0.9)
```
Field is slow because gates are cheap to retrace and the magnet is not — the magnet ramps once, monotonically, across the whole fan. Every lock-in X/P read at each grid point. Analysis side plots B vs n (`pcolormesh`) per contact pair and overlays Středa lines (see Verify). Distinct from its two neighbors: `field-sweep-1d` is one gate point with full B-axis density; `gatemap-in-field` is the full 2D gate plane at a *single* B. The fan trades both for the (n, B) plane — the only measurement that resolves how gapped states *disperse* with field.

## When
Three triggers, in rough campaign order:
- **Oscillation check** — a `field-sweep-1d` or `gatemap-in-field` showed quantum-oscillation-like wiggles and you need to know if they're real. The corpus idiom is literally named for this: RPL_19's "Small fan to check if oscillations are real" (a 161 × 151 fan after an effective-mass series kept hinting at SdH). A feature that moves systematically across the n-line as B steps is physics; one that doesn't is noise or gate drift.
- **State classification** — a map shows a vanishing-ρxx region (or a busy set of dips) and the discriminating question is whether the features disperse. This is the classification backbone of an FQAH/SC-style campaign (arXiv 2504.06972: ρxx(ν_h, B) fans + Středa fits are how (R/F/I)QAH states were separated from the SC region).
- **Calibration** — SdH/LL frequency vs n gives cap ratios independently of the CNP-slope method, and for a moiré device the fan anchors the moiré density n_M. The extraction is `cap-ratio-calibration`'s job (deferred — recipe not yet written); the fan is its input data.

Prerequisites are `nD-map`'s plus a field-verified magnet: cap ratios `dtg`/`dbg` must be trusted (the fast axis is a line in (n, D) — wrong caps tilt it), and the field source must be live (Yokogawa cache seeded after kernel restart, AMI430 in operating mode — see `field-sweep-1d` plumbing notes).

A dip in ρxx at one B value is ambiguous — gap, SC, contact artifact, density wobble. One measurement, three discriminations, plus calibration for free.

The cost is real: these are the most expensive sweeps in the corpus. Aaron's inline arithmetic (`(351*501)/(201*151)*3` in 20260124 cell 134) is the toploader-era form.

**Estimate before you run — the full cost model**: wall-clock = **field-traverse time + N_rows × (row turnaround + N_fast × per-point time)**. Which term dominates is a rig property, not a constant of nature: **if the field source is ramp-rate-limited and the set call blocks** (check the rig card for whether yours is), the traverse term is fixed by the B-span alone — **finer B steps cost only row turnaround, and coarsening B buys aliasing, not time**. A "free" measured ramp-down is usually still worth taking — it buys data for wall-clock — but it is not free: price it at the measured rate, from the rig card's Timing rules (`rig_card.md`), never the bare one. Calibrate row turnaround and per-point time from this session's own first sweeps; inherited timing constants carry a provenance tag and the conditions they were measured under, or they are guesses.

Excitation: Aaron runs 1 V (graphene-scale) and bumps to 2.5 V for 12 T work; on a fragile-state device (FQAH/SC, arXiv 2504.06972's 1 nA cap) respect the device-card excitation ceiling instead — the states you're classifying wash out if heated.
4. Build the slow field axis: a **per-column SdH-FFT fan** uses `B_vec = field_invB(B_start, B_end, N)` (uniform in 1/B, both > 0); a **Středa/SC fan** uses `np.linspace` and may start at 0. Position the magnet at the fan's start field and let it settle: `s.ramp(mag.field, B_start)` then `time.sleep(600)` for multi-tesla positioning (RPL_19/20260217 cells 88/94), `time.sleep(30)` at ~1 T (RPL_10), `time.sleep(5*60)` at 0.6 T (20260124 cell 235). Plan the direction (endpoint order) so the fan *starts* where the magnet already is and *ends* where the next measurement needs it — never re-traverse. The elevated-T fan covers ±5 T as four chained segments (5→0.6, 0.6→0, 0→−0.6, −0.6→−5; 20260124 cells 239–242), each starting where the last ended.
5. Build `s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)`. `s.add_comment('landau-fan')` then a structured tag: `s.add_comment(f'D = {D0} V/nm, n = {n_lo} to {n_hi}, B = {B_start} to {B_end} T')`, plus `s.add_comment(grab_metadata())` where available. **Watch out** — RPL_10's fans carry exemplary comments (`'MC4, Vsi = -20V, quantum oscillations, D = 0.31 V/nm, n = -2.9 to -2.1, B = 1 to 0 T'`); RPL_19's fan cells carry *none* (files 1776/1840 have empty `comments`) — only a stale `# 1776` Python comment. The recipe asks for the RPL_10 discipline.
6. `s.ramp(sr830_1.amplitude, A)`, `s.ramp(k_si.volt, V_si)`, `s.ramp(bias_voltage.volt, 0)` if present. `fp` temperature(s) and every lock-in X/P; `plot` gate currents for live leakage (`s.plot(k_bg.volt, k_bg.curr)`, `s.plot('time', k_tg.curr)`, `s.plot('time', k_si.curr)` — RPL_19 fan idiom; note `fp` of gate currents is often omitted here, so leakage lands in the live plot but *not* in the TSV).
7. The sweep (step 0 call above). Delay band in the corpus: `slow_delay=1` (gates retrace during it; the field step itself is rate-limited by the magnet), `fast_delay` ≈ 4τ default — a Středa/dispersion fan tolerates the uniform fast-axis lag like a slope; ~6τ when the n-axis carries the extracted signal (per-column SdH FFT, or coarse n), where the lag distorts it, with denser n trading against the dwell.
8. Park gates (`k_bg.volt(0); k_tg.volt(0)`), decide the field endpoint deliberately (leave it for a follow-up fan, `s.ramp(mag.field, 0)`, or ride home as a measured traverse — a free `field-sweep-1d`, priced at the measured rate per the Why cost model), and ping (`alerts.discord('🐍jobs done🐍')`) — at 5–30 h these runs outlive operator attention spans.

## Verify
Disk-side checks, then the Středa read. The fan is unrolled into flat rows; the slow column is `magnet_field`.

```python
from hera.analysis import open_run, summarize_run
import numpy as np

run = open_run("<notebook_dir>/data/<file_id>")
print(summarize_run(run))
# expect: type 2D, recipe 'landau-fan', slow_param ['magnet_field'],
#         fast_param ['k_tg_volt', 'k_bg_volt'].

# 1. Completeness — at 5-30 h these are the most interruption-prone sweeps
#    in the corpus (RPL_10 file 158 and TD48-era runs died early; Aaron
#    re-ran rather than salvaged).
assert not run.interrupted, "fan was interrupted; decide re-run vs salvage with the human"

# 2. B axis actually traversed the plan, monotonically per segment.
B = run.col("magnet_field")
print(f"B traversed: {B.min():.3f} → {B.max():.3f} T over {len(run.meta['slow_setpoints'][0])} steps")

# 3. Fast axis is a paired n-line: both gate columns move together.
vtg, vbg = run.col("k_tg_volt"), run.col("k_bg_volt")
assert np.ptp(vtg) > 0 and np.ptp(vbg) > 0, "one gate is frozen — not a paired n-line"

# 4. Temperature stayed at base across the fan (a 30 h run spans fridge
#    events). NOTE: 20260124-era RPL_19 data has TWO columns literally
#    named 'T' (probe + fridge); later sessions rename to T_probe/T_fridge.
#    run.col('T') raises on the duplicate — use col_indices/col_at.
for tname in ("T_probe", "T"):
    idxs = run.col_indices(tname)
    if idxs:
        T = run.col_at(idxs[0])
        print(f"{tname}: {np.nanmin(T)*1e3:.0f}–{np.nanmax(T)*1e3:.0f} mK")
        break

# 5. Lock-ins not flat/NaN (same as gatemap). Gate-current columns are
#    usually ABSENT in fan data (plot-only, step 6) — skip, don't fail.
for name in set(run.cols):
    if name.startswith("sr830_") and name.endswith("_X"):
        x = run.col_at(run.col_indices(name)[0])
        if np.allclose(x, x[0]) or np.isnan(x).any():
            print(f"⚠️  {name} flat or NaN — check sensitivity/wiring")
```

- A linearly dispersing dip is a gapped state with Chern number `C = (h/e) · dn/dB` (n in absolute units). The corpus tools are inline in the ana notebooks: `streda()` returning `B = phi0 * n / C` (RPL_19/20251220_ana cells 96–98) and the overlay form `x_fit = C * y_fit * 1E-16 / (h/e)` plotted over the file-1840 fan (20260124_ana cell 93, C = 1 dashed line with the constants from the boilerplate cell 3).
- **Moiré devices**: the slope converts to a Chern number only through the moiré density — `C = (h/e) · n_M · dν_h/dB`. The corpus has no ν_h layer; anchoring n_M and the ν_h↔n conversion is `cap-ratio-calibration`'s job (deferred — recipe not yet written). Until it exists, report slopes in raw dn/dB and flag the assignment.
- **Do not hard-code "plateau value ⇒ Středa slope"** [flagged for expert review]: the RIQAH states in arXiv 2504.06972 show ρxy quantized at h/e² while their ρxx dips disperse with slopes near their *fractional filling*, not C = 1 — explicitly unexplained in that paper. A plateau/dispersion mismatch is an escalate-to-expert finding, not a fit error.
- **Fan onset as a quality metric**: the lowest B at which oscillations/LL dips resolve tracks quantum mobility — RPL_10's fans resolved structure below 1 T; RPL_19's oscillation check needed 0.9–2.5 T. A later cooldown whose onset field moves up is a device-quality regression worth noting.

- `aaron/RPL_19/20260124_measure.ipynb` cells 117–119, 173–176, 234–242, 278–284 — the mature fan family. **Cell-range adjustment vs. index**: the brief cited the "Small fan to check if oscillations are real" as ~cells 167–176; actually 167–172 are still `# Resuming effective mass` (higher field range), the small-fan section is header 173, base-recool cell 174 (`heater.volt(0)` + 1 h `interruptible_sleep`), fans 175 (D = 0.2) and 176 (D = 1) — 161 B steps 0.9→2.5 T × 151-pt n-line, `fast_delay=0.6` → file 1776, 5.5 h, the `after-qo-confirmed` fixture cut. Cells 234–242 are the deep fan (cell 236 → file 1840: 441 × 231, 0.6→5 T, 30.1 h) plus the `## Elevated T Fan` (heater at 2.75 V, 20-min settle, designer hstack n-vector, ±5 T in four chained segments). # Trilayer FS-count forward model — ABA vs ABC

Backs the `recipes/investigations/trilayer-stacking-fs-count.md` investigation.
Where `models/aba_trilayer/` computes the **Landau-fan crossing structure** (the
Datta fingerprint), this model computes the **B = 0 Fermi-surface count** and the
**Onsager frequencies** the FS-count read overlays on data: ABA ≥ 2 coexisting
surfaces (ML Dirac + BL parabolic) vs ABC's single post-Lifshitz pocket.

The survey that grounds it (band structure, the three ingested papers, the
feasibility numbers) is `docs/stacking-extraction-survey.md`; read it for the
physics. This README covers what the tools are and how to run them.

## Files

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `fs_count_b0.py` | B = 0 FS count + Onsager F(n, D). **ABA** from the continuum 6-site SWMcC Hamiltonian (Datta params, γ₃=γ₄=0 — same parameters as `models/aba_trilayer/ll_spectrum.py`); **ABC** from the MacDonald PRB 82, 035409 (2010) effective two-band model (Eq. 6/7) with trigonal warping → the 3-pocket → annulus → single-pocket Lifshitz cascade. Counts distinct extremal-orbit frequencies F = (ℏ/2πe)·A_k. Pure numpy/scipy. |
| `plots.py` | Renders `{aba_bands_linecut, abc_bands_linecut, abc_bands_contour, luttinger_vs_n}.png` from `fs_count_b0`. |
| `ll_sequence.py` | High-field complement: ABA Landau-level fan + QH/Streda sequence (the pseudo-decoupled ML Dirac band offsets the Chern sequence; non-dispersing ML N=0 doublet). Imports the validated `models/aba_trilayer/ll_spectrum.py`. Outputs `aba_LL_fan.png`, `aba_wannier.png`. |
| `*.png` | Generated figures (band linecuts, ABC contour, Luttinger-sum check, LL fan, Wannier diagram). |
| `rmg-fft-snapshot/` | Frozen copy of the RMG SdH-FFT analysis pipeline (background-subtract in B → interp to 1/B → window → FFT, with the stability-sweep hygiene). A **reference snapshot, not a standalone package** — see its `PROVENANCE.md`; reconcile into `hera.analysis.sdh_fft` later. |

## Run

```bash
cd hera/models/trilayer_fs_count
uv run --no-project --with numpy --with scipy python3 fs_count_b0.py              # FS count + Onsager frequencies
uv run --no-project --with numpy --with scipy --with matplotlib python3 plots.py # band/Luttinger figures
uv run --no-project --with numpy --with scipy --with matplotlib python3 ll_sequence.py  # high-field Streda fan
```
(`--no-project` pulls just numpy/scipy/matplotlib — the worktree's submodules
aren't checked out, so `uv sync` can't run here.)

## Validation

- **Luttinger sum** Σf = n at the right degeneracy reproduces in both models at
  every density tested — the model-independent consistency check on the count.
- `fs_count_b0` reproduces MacDonald's trigonal-warping Lifshitz cascade location
  (~10¹¹ cm⁻²), so ABC presents a single Fermi surface at the ~10¹² operating
  density.
- `ll_sequence` builds on the already-validated `aba_trilayer/ll_spectrum.py`
  (the 2 meV / 14 meV band splittings gate that model).

## Gap / future work

A quantitative **ABC** Landau-level model is **not yet built** — only ABA is
computed, so the high-field Streda/Chern contrast (recipe Step 6) is qualitative
on the ABC side. See `docs/stacking-extraction-survey.md` §9. A candidate
implementation to adapt is Dan Parker's `RhombohedralGrapheneLandau.jl`, though
it appears R4G (tetralayer)-specific and would need trilayer adaptation.

**Onsager F(n) is numerically clamped above |n| ≈ 3.5e12 cm⁻²** (`aba_fs` E_F
search capped at 70 meV; `abc_fs` a 50 meV window + `kmax`): above the density
the energy/k grid reaches, `np.interp` clamps to the grid edge instead of
failing, so F(n) **flattens spuriously**. This is a solver-domain artifact, *not*
a model-validity limit. Consequence: the curves do not reach the QC0426 operating
density (±8e12), so the Step-5 overlay cannot currently be run at the operating
point. **TODO (Aaron + Claude to revisit):** extend the grids to cover the
operating range, and/or make the solver raise/NaN above its covered range rather
than silently clamp.

# === Gate C: gate-current sanity check — Cell A (4 legs, one file each) ===
# Preconditions (state this cell assumes but does not set)
_T = T_sample(); _B = magnet.field()
print(f"precheck: T_sample = {_T:.3f} K (expect < 2), B = {_B:+.4f} T (expect ~0), "
      f"Vtg = {k_tg.volt():+.3f}, Vbg = {k_bg.volt():+.3f}, Vsi = {dc205.voltage():+.3f}")
assert _T < 2.0, "not at base T"
assert abs(_B) < 0.05, "magnet not at zero"
assert abs(k_tg.volt()) < 1e-3 and abs(k_bg.volt()) < 1e-3, "gates not parked at 0"

legs = [
    (k_tg, TG_MAX), (k_tg, TG_MIN),   # +3 / -3 V (SAFETIES limits)
    (k_bg, BG_MAX), (k_bg, BG_MIN),   # +4.5 / -4.5 V
]
n_pts = 251
delay = 1  # s; > 4*tau settling floor (tau = 0.3 s, 24 dB/oct)
lockins = [sr0, sr1, sr2, sr3]

# pA-floor gate-current readback; reset cell restores nplci=1
k_tg.nplci(10)
k_bg.nplci(10)

for gate, v_endpoint in legs:
    s = sweep.AsyncStation(meas_config)
    s.add_comment('gate-current-sanity-check')
    s.add_comment(f'gate: {gate.name}, leg: 0 -> {v_endpoint:+g} V (card limit); '
                  f'other gate 0, Vsi = 0, B = 0, T = {_T:.2f} K, I_bias = 5 nA')

    s.ramp(k_tg.volt, 0)
    s.ramp(k_bg.volt, 0)

    xp = gate.volt
    s.fp(T_sample)
    s.fp(k_tg.volt).fp(k_tg.curr)
    s.fp(k_bg.volt).fp(k_bg.curr)
    s.plot(xp, k_tg.curr)
    s.plot(xp, k_bg.curr)
    for lia in lockins:
        s.fp(lia.X).fp(lia.P)
        s.plot(xp, lia.X)

    try:
        s.sweep(gate.volt, np.linspace(0, v_endpoint, n_pts), delay=delay)
    finally:
        s.ramp(gate.volt, 0)

print("all legs done; gates parked at 0")

"""Gate C liveness analysis — runs 0-3 (gate-current-sanity-check)."""
import numpy as np
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from hera.analysis import open_run

I_BIAS = 5e-9
SR0_GAIN = -1e6
LEGS = [("data/0", "TG 0->+3 V"), ("data/1", "TG 0->-3 V"),
        ("data/2", "BG 0->+4.5 V"), ("data/3", "BG 0->-4.5 V")]

fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 4, figsize=(16, 9), sharex="col")
for j, (d, title) in enumerate(LEGS):
    run = open_run(d)
    swept = "k_2400_tg_volt" if "TG" in title else "k_2400_bg_volt"
    v = run.col_at(run.col_indices(swept)[0])  # setpoint column
    itg = run.col_at(run.col_indices("k_2400_tg_curr")[-1])
    ibg = run.col_at(run.col_indices("k_2400_bg_curr")[-1])
    sr0x = run.col_at(run.col_indices("sr0_X")[-1])
    i_drain = sr0x / SR0_GAIN

    # row 0: raw drain current
    ax = axes[0, j]
    ax.plot(v, i_drain * 1e9, lw=0.8, color="k")
    ax.set_title(title)
    ax.set_ylabel("I_drain (nA)" if j == 0 else "")
    ax.set_ylim(0, 6)

    # row 1: 4T resistances
    ax = axes[1, j]
    for ch, lbl in (("sr1_X", "sr1 T3-T4"), ("sr2_X", "sr2 B4-B5"), ("sr3_X", "sr3 T5-B6 (xy)")):
        x = run.col_at(run.col_indices(ch)[-1])
        ax.plot(v, x / I_BIAS, lw=0.8, label=lbl)
    ax.set_yscale("symlog", linthresh=10)
    ax.set_ylabel("R = X/I (Ohm)" if j == 0 else "")
    if j == 0:
        ax.legend(fontsize=7)

    # row 2: gate currents
    ax = axes[2, j]
    ax.plot(v, itg * 1e12, lw=0.8, label="I_tg")
    ax.plot(v, ibg * 1e12, lw=0.8, label="I_bg")
    ax.set_ylabel("I_gate (pA)" if j == 0 else "")
    ax.set_xlabel("swept gate (V)")
    ax.set_ylim(-150, 150)
    if j == 0:
        ax.legend(fontsize=7)

    print(f"{d} {title}: I_drain {i_drain.min()*1e9:.2f}-{i_drain.max()*1e9:.2f} nA, "
          f"|I_tg|max {np.abs(itg).max()*1e12:.0f} pA, |I_bg|max {np.abs(ibg).max()*1e12:.0f} pA, "
          f"interrupted={run.interrupted}")

fig.suptitle("Gate C liveness — gate-current-sanity-check, runs 0-3 (B=0, T=1.15 K, I_bias=5 nA)")
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig("hera_scratch/gatec_liveness.png", dpi=110)
print("saved hera_scratch/gatec_liveness.png")

import numpy as np
```python
import scipy.constants as cst
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

from pathlib import Path

from hera.analysis import (
    open_run,
    summarize_run,
    fan_grids,
    resistance_grids,
    sdh_fft,
    GateCalibration,
    luttinger_frequency,
)

%matplotlib inline


def _resolve_data_dir():
    """Locate this run's ./data dir from the notebook's own location.

    The ana kernel's cwd is not guaranteed to be the measurement dir, so a
    bare './data' breaks loaders with FileNotFoundError. IPython sets
    globals()['_dh'] to a list whose first entry is the notebook's startup
    cwd (the dir holding the notebook); this survives jupyter-collaboration/
    RTC and any later %cd, so we prefer it. We fall back to Path.cwd() and
    search a few levels up so loading still works if the kernel started inside
    ./data/<id>/. The walk stops before the filesystem root so an unrelated
    top-level 'data' dir can never be matched.
    """
    candidates = []
    dh = globals().get("_dh")
    if dh:
        candidates.append(Path(dh[0]))
    candidates.append(Path.cwd())
    for base in candidates:
        base = Path(base).resolve()
        for d in [base, *base.parents]:
            if d == d.parent:  # filesystem root
                break
            cand = d / "data"
            if cand.is_dir():
                return str(cand)
    return str((Path(candidates[0]) / "data").resolve())


file_path = _resolve_data_dir()


# Open a run by id: run(119) -> Run. Run.col(name) for a column;
# summarize_run(run(119)) for a recipe / range / completeness / T glance.
def run(i):
    return open_run(Path(file_path) / str(i))
```

## (n, D) — capacitance-based convention

`GateCalibration` carries the gate->(n, D) lever arm: `cal.n_D(V_tg, V_bg)`
returns `n` in SI (m^-2; ×1e-16 for 10^12 cm^-2) and `D` in V/m. Build it from
the gate-stack thicknesses with `from_thicknesses` (κ_hBN/κ_SiO2 default).
This is the capacitance convention, **not** the toploader's `dtg/dbg` constant
form. Set `n_offset` / `D_offset` from `cnp-and-dline-calibration` once the CNP
/ D-line is live.

```python
t_bg = 12e-9     # back-gate hBN thickness, m    # <-- validate

# Session gate calibration. cal.n_D(V_tg, V_bg) -> (n [m^-2], D [V/m]);
# set n_offset / D_offset from cnp-and-dline-calibration once live.
cal = GateCalibration.from_thicknesses(t_tg, t_bg, t_bgSiO2)
```

## HERA — Step 1: 0 T gate map (`gatemap`) for CNP line + (n, D) calibration

Gate C passed (runs 0–3, verdict in ana). Next per the governing investigation (`trilayer-stacking-fs-count` Step 1): the 0 T TG–BG map that `cnp-and-dline-calibration` consumes — CNP ridge per channel → capacitance ratio from the slope → the (n, D) conversion, plus the region survey (clean hole/electron sides, D = 0 line, contact arms staying metallic).

**Design.** TG fast −3 → +3 V, **121 pts (50 mV step)** — Gate C shows the CNP peak ~0.5 V wide, so ≥10 pts across it; BG slow −3 → +3 V, **61 rows (0.1 V step)**. BG is clipped at ±3 V (not the ±4.5 card limit) because the geometry-prior slope (−c_bg/c_tg ≈ −1.3) walks the ridge out of the TG window at |Vbg| ≈ 2.7 V — rows beyond that carry no ridge and little else; the price of full BG coverage would be ~+1.2 h for edge-clipped rows. D = 0 reach on this map: |n| up to ~6×10¹² cm⁻² (geometry prior).

**Sensitivities**: sr1–sr3 stay at 2e-5 (card CNP scale; rails above ~4 kΩ — a railed ridge row is expected at larger |D| and the calibration fit handles it via outlier rejection). sr0 bumped 5 mV → **10 mV** for headroom (it sits at 99.7 % of range at full 5 nA; the card's metallic-regime setting).

**Cost** (calibrated on runs 0–3: 2.13 s/pt at delay = 1 → ~2.4 s/pt at fast_delay = 1.2): 61 × 121 = 7 381 pts ≈ 4.9 h + ~15 min row turnaround → **~5–5.5 h** (overnight run; done ≈ 03:00). Checkpoints: first 3 rows (~15 min in — leakage, railing, dead channel), then mid-run.

Preconditions asserted in-cell: T < 2 K, |B| < 0.05 T, Si at 0 V, gates at 0. Gates park at 0 on completion.

# === Step 1: 0 T gate map — TG fast (121 pts, -3..+3), BG slow (61 rows, -3..+3) ===
_T = T_sample(); _B = magnet.field()
print(f"precheck: T={_T:.3f} K (<2), B={_B:+.4f} T (~0), Vtg={k_tg.volt():+.3f}, "
      f"Vbg={k_bg.volt():+.3f}, Vsi={dc205.voltage():+.3f} (all ~0)")
assert _T < 2.0 and abs(_B) < 0.05
assert abs(k_tg.volt()) < 1e-3 and abs(k_bg.volt()) < 1e-3 and abs(dc205.voltage()) < 1e-3

# sr0 headroom: 5 nA x 1 MOhm = 5 mV sits at 99.7% of the 5 mV range -> 10 mV
sr0.sensitivity(10e-3)

vtg_fast = np.linspace(-3.0, 3.0, 121)   # 50 mV step, inside validators
vbg_slow = np.linspace(-3.0, 3.0, 61)    # 0.1 V step, ridge in-window to |Vbg|~2.7

s = sweep.AsyncStation(meas_config)
s.add_comment('gatemap')
s.add_comment(f'TG fast -3..+3 (121 pts), BG slow -3..+3 (61 rows), Vsi=0, B=0, '
              f'T={_T:.2f} K, I_bias=5 nA, sens sr1-3 2e-5 / sr0 1e-2, fast_delay=1.2 (4 tau)')

s.ramp(k_tg.volt, vtg_fast[0])
s.ramp(k_bg.volt, vbg_slow[0])

s.fp(T_sample)
s.fp(k_tg.volt).fp(k_tg.curr)
s.fp(k_bg.volt).fp(k_bg.curr)
s.plot(k_tg.volt, k_tg.curr)      # live leakage, swept gate
s.plot('time', k_bg.curr)         # live leakage, stepped gate
for lia in (sr0, sr1, sr2, sr3):
    s.fp(lia.X).fp(lia.P)
    s.plot(k_tg.volt, lia.X)

try:
    s.megasweep(k_bg.volt, vbg_slow, k_tg.volt, vtg_fast,
                slow_delay=3, fast_delay=1.2)
finally:
    s.ramp(k_tg.volt, 0)
    s.ramp(k_bg.volt, 0)
print("gatemap done; gates parked at 0")

"""CNP-line calibration from run 4 (cnp-and-dline-calibration)."""
import numpy as np
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter1d
from hera.analysis import open_run, fan_grids, resistance_grids, GateCalibration

run = open_run("data/4")
fg = fan_grids(run)
rg = resistance_grids(fg)
vbg = fg.slow                     # 61 rows
vtg = np.asarray(fg.grid("k_2400_tg_volt"))[0] if hasattr(fg, "grid") else None
# fast-axis vector: take from first row of the tg grid
vtg_grid = np.asarray(fg.grid("k_2400_tg_volt"))
vtg = vtg_grid[0]
print("grid:", vtg_grid.shape, "vbg:", vbg.shape, "vtg:", vtg[:3], "...", vtg[-3:])
print("R channels:", list(rg.R.keys()) if hasattr(rg.R, "keys") else type(rg.R))

RAIL = 4.3e3  # 2e-5 rail at 5 nA ~ 4.37 kOhm
results = {}
for ch in ("sr1", "sr2"):
    R = np.asarray(rg.R[ch])
    ridge_v, keep_rows = [], []
    for i in range(R.shape[0]):
        row = gaussian_filter1d(R[i], 2)
        j = int(np.argmax(row))
        railed = np.sum(R[i] > RAIL) >= 3
        edge = j <= 2 or j >= len(row) - 3
        # rail plateau: use center of plateau instead of argmax
        if railed:
            idx = np.where(R[i] > RAIL)[0]
            if idx.max() - idx.min() < 20:            # contiguous-ish plateau
                j = int(np.round(idx.mean()))
                edge = j <= 2 or j >= len(row) - 3
            else:
                ridge_v.append(np.nan); keep_rows.append(False); continue
        ridge_v.append(vtg[j])
        keep_rows.append(not edge)
    ridge_v = np.array(ridge_v); keep = np.array(keep_rows)
    # iterative robust fit
    k = keep & np.isfinite(ridge_v)
    for _ in range(4):
        p = np.polyfit(vbg[k], ridge_v[k], 1)
        res = ridge_v - np.polyval(p, vbg)
        s = np.nanstd(res[k])
        k_new = keep & np.isfinite(ridge_v) & (np.abs(res) < 2 * s)
        if k_new.sum() == k.sum(): break
        k = k_new
    results[ch] = dict(slope=p[0], intercept=p[1], resid_rms=float(np.nanstd(res[k])),
                       nrows=int(k.sum()), ridge=ridge_v, keep=k)
    print(f"{ch}: slope {p[0]:+.4f}, intercept {p[1]:+.4f} V, resid rms {np.nanstd(res[k])*1e3:.1f} mV, rows {k.sum()}/61")

# geometry prior ratio
print("geometry prior c_bg/c_tg = 15.6/12 =", 15.6/12)

"""CNP calibration — overlay figure + closure + calibration numbers."""
import numpy as np
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter1d
from scipy.constants import epsilon_0, e as qe
from hera.analysis import open_run, fan_grids, resistance_grids, GateCalibration

run = open_run("data/4")
fg = fan_grids(run)
rg = resistance_grids(fg)
vbg = fg.slow
vtg = np.asarray(fg.grid("k_2400_tg_volt"))[0]
RAIL = 4.3e3

def extract(ch):
    R = np.asarray(rg.R[ch])
    ridge_v, keep = [], []
    for i in range(R.shape[0]):
        row = gaussian_filter1d(R[i], 2)
        j = int(np.argmax(row))
        railed = np.sum(R[i] > RAIL) >= 3
        if railed:
            idx = np.where(R[i] > RAIL)[0]
            if idx.max() - idx.min() < 20:
                j = int(np.round(idx.mean()))
            else:
                ridge_v.append(np.nan); keep.append(False); continue
        edge = j <= 2 or j >= len(row) - 3
        ridge_v.append(vtg[j]); keep.append(not edge)
    ridge_v = np.array(ridge_v); keep = np.array(keep)
    k = keep & np.isfinite(ridge_v)
    for _ in range(4):
        p = np.polyfit(vbg[k], ridge_v[k], 1)
        res = ridge_v - np.polyval(p, vbg)
        s = np.nanstd(res[k])
        k2 = keep & np.isfinite(ridge_v) & (np.abs(res) < 2 * s)
        if k2.sum() == k.sum(): break
        k = k2
    return ridge_v, k, p

fits = {ch: extract(ch) for ch in ("sr1", "sr2")}

# --- calibration: anchor c_tg at geometry (AFM 15.6 nm hBN), ratio from mean slope
c_tg = epsilon_0 * 3 / 15.6e-9
ratio = -np.mean([fits["sr1"][2][0], fits["sr2"][2][0]])
c_bg = ratio * c_tg
b = np.mean([fits["sr1"][2][1], fits["sr2"][2][1]])
n_cnp = c_tg * b / qe                       # m^-2 at (b, 0)
cal = GateCalibration(c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=-(-n_cnp))  # n_offset so n=0 on ridge
# careful with sign: n(Vtg,Vbg) = (c_tg Vtg + c_bg Vbg)/e + n_offset; want n=0 at Vtg=b,Vbg=0
n_offset = -c_tg * b / qe
cal = GateCalibration(c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=n_offset)

# closure: n along fitted ridge (sr-mean line)
vv = np.linspace(-2.6, 2.6, 53)
ridge_line = b - ratio * vv
n_resid, D_line = cal.n_D(ridge_line, vv)
print(f"ratio c_bg/c_tg = {ratio:.4f} (geometry prior 1.300, per-ch {-fits['sr1'][2][0]:.4f}/{-fits['sr2'][2][0]:.4f})")
print(f"c_tg = {c_tg:.4e} F/m^2 (anchor, geometry), c_bg = {c_bg:.4e} F/m^2 (ratio-calibrated)")
print(f"intercept b = {b:+.4f} V -> n_offset = {n_offset:.3e} m^-2 = {n_offset*1e-16:+.3f} e12 cm^-2")
print(f"closure: max|n| along ridge = {np.abs(n_resid).max()*1e-16:.4f} e12 cm^-2")
print(f"D along ridge spans {D_line.min()/1e9:.3f} .. {D_line.max()/1e9:.3f} V/nm")

# D=0 reach with validators
from sharpelab_nb.gates import calc_gate_voltages
ns = np.linspace(-8e16, 8e16, 401)
Vt, Vb = calc_gate_voltages(ns, np.zeros_like(ns), c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=n_offset)
ok = (np.abs(Vt) <= 3.0) & (np.abs(Vb) <= 4.5)
print(f"D=0 realized n-window: {ns[ok].min()*1e-16:+.2f} .. {ns[ok].max()*1e-16:+.2f} e12 cm^-2")

# --- figure: maps + ridge + fits
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 4, figsize=(19, 4.6), sharey=True)
for ax, ch in zip(axes[:2], ("sr1", "sr2")):
    R = np.asarray(rg.R[ch])
    pm = ax.pcolormesh(vtg, vbg, np.log10(np.clip(R, 10, None)), cmap="inferno", shading="auto")
    plt.colorbar(pm, ax=ax, label="log10 R (Ohm)")
    rv, k, p = fits[ch]
    ax.plot(rv[k], vbg[k], "c.", ms=3)
    ax.plot(np.polyval(p, vbg), vbg, "c-", lw=0.7)
    ax.set_title(f"{ch}: slope {p[0]:+.3f}, b {p[1]:+.3f} V")
    ax.set_xlabel("V_tg (V)"); ax.set_xlim(-3, 3)
I0 = np.asarray(rg.current) if not isinstance(rg.current, dict) else np.asarray(rg.current["sr0"])
pm = axes[2].pcolormesh(vtg, vbg, I0 * 1e9, cmap="viridis", shading="auto")
plt.colorbar(pm, ax=axes[2], label="I_drain (nA)")
axes[2].set_title("sr0 drain current"); axes[2].set_xlabel("V_tg (V)")
R3 = np.asarray(rg.R["sr3"])
pm = axes[3].pcolormesh(vtg, vbg, np.clip(R3, -50, 400), cmap="RdBu_r", shading="auto")
plt.colorbar(pm, ax=axes[3], label="R_xy (Ohm)")
axes[3].set_title("sr3 (Rxy @ B=0)"); axes[3].set_xlabel("V_tg (V)")
axes[0].set_ylabel("V_bg (V)")
fig.suptitle("run 4 — 0 T gatemap: CNP ridge + fits (cyan), drain current, Hall channel")
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig("hera_scratch/cnp_cal_map.png", dpi=110)
print("saved hera_scratch/cnp_cal_map.png")
